requirements.text: MQTT requires an ordered, lossless, bidirectional transport; TCP port 1883 is registered for MQTT.

source_ref.quote: The MQTT protocol requires an underlying transport that provides an ordered, lossless, stream of bytes from the Client to Server and Server to Client. […] TCP ports 8883 and 1883 are registered with IANA for MQTT TLS and non TLS communication respectively.

requirements.text: An MQTT UTF-8 string has a two-byte big-endian length prefix followed by well-formed UTF-8 data.

source_ref.section: 1.5.2 Integer data values; 1.5.3 UTF-8 encoded strings
source_ref.quote: Integer data values are 16 bits in big-endian order: the high order byte precedes the lower order byte. […] Each of these strings is prefixed with a two byte length field that gives the number of bytes in a UTF-8 encoded string itself, as illustrated in Figure 1.1 Structure of UTF-8 encoded strings below. […] The character data in a UTF-8 encoded string MUST be well-formed UTF-8 as defined by the Unicode specification [Unicode] and restated in RFC 3629 [RFC3629].

requirements.text: Remaining Length MUST use the MQTT variable byte integer encoding and equal the bytes after the fixed header.

source_ref.quote: The Remaining Length is the number of bytes remaining within the current packet, including data in the variable header and the payload. The Remaining Length does not include the bytes used to encode the Remaining Length. […] The Remaining Length is encoded using a variable length encoding scheme which uses a single byte for values up to 127.

requirements.text: Every Control Packet MUST use its assigned type code and reserved fixed-header flags; invalid flags cause the connection to close.

source_ref.quote: Position: byte 1, bits 7-4. Represented as a 4-bit unsigned value, the values are listed in Table 2.1 - Control packet types. […] Where a flag bit is marked as “Reserved” in Table 2.2 - Flag Bits, it is reserved for future use and MUST be set to the value listed in that table [MQTT-2.2.2-1]. If invalid flags are received, the receiver MUST close the Network Connection [MQTT-2.2.2-2].

requirements.text: CONNECT MUST encode Protocol Name MQTT and be the first packet sent by a client.

source_ref.quote: After a Network Connection is established by a Client to a Server, the first Packet sent from the Client to the Server MUST be a CONNECT Packet [MQTT-3.1.0-1]. […] The Protocol Name is a UTF-8 encoded string that represents the protocol name “MQTT”, capitalized as shown.

requirements.text: A broker receiving protocol_level other than 4 MUST send CONNACK return code 1 and then close.

source_ref.quote: The Server MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet with a CONNACK return code 0x01 (unacceptable protocol level) and then disconnect the Client if the Protocol Level is not supported by the Server [MQTT-3.1.2-2].

requirements.text: The selected M0 scope fixes clean_session to 1 and excludes Will, user name, and password.

source_ref.section: 3.1.2.4 Clean Session; 3.1.2.5 Will Flag; 3.1.2.8 User Name Flag; 3.1.2.9 Password Flag
source_ref.quote: If CleanSession is set to 1, the Client and Server MUST discard any previous Session and start a new one. […] If the Will Flag is set to 0 the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect Flags MUST be set to zero and the Will Topic and Will Message fields MUST NOT be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-11]. […] If the User Name Flag is set to 0, a user name MUST NOT be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-18]. […] If the Password Flag is set to 0, a password MUST NOT be present in the payload [MQTT-3.1.2-20].

requirements.text: The selected M0 client identifier is 1 to 23 alphanumeric UTF-8 bytes.

source_ref.quote: The Server MUST allow ClientIds which are between 1 and 23 UTF-8 encoded bytes in length, and that contain only the characters "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ" [MQTT-3.1.3-5].

requirements.text: A valid clean-session CONNECT MUST receive CONNACK with session_present 0 and return_code 0.

source_ref.quote: If the Server accepts a connection with CleanSession set to 1, the Server MUST set Session Present to 0 in the CONNACK packet in addition to setting a zero return code in the CONNACK packet [MQTT-3.2.2-1].

requirements.text: The selected M0 PUBLISH form uses QoS 0, DUP 0, RETAIN 0 and carries the topic name and application payload.

source_ref.section: 3.3.1 PUBLISH Fixed header; 3.3.2.1 Topic Name; 3.3.3 Payload
source_ref.quote: The DUP flag MUST be set to 0 for all QoS 0 messages [MQTT-3.3.1-2]. […] 0 0 0 At most once delivery […] If the RETAIN flag is 0, in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Client to a Server, the Server MUST NOT store the message and MUST NOT remove or replace any existing retained message [MQTT-3.3.1-12]. […] The Topic Name MUST be present as the first field in the PUBLISH Packet Variable header. It MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string [MQTT-3.3.2-1] as defined in section 1.5.3. […] The Payload contains the Application Message that is being published.

requirements.text: SUBSCRIBE MUST contain a non-zero Packet Identifier and one or more Topic Filter/requested QoS entries.

source_ref.quote: SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PUBLISH (in cases where QoS > 0) Control Packets MUST contain a non-zero 16-bit Packet Identifier [MQTT-2.3.1-1]. […] The payload of a SUBSCRIBE packet MUST contain at least one Topic Filter / QoS pair. A SUBSCRIBE packet with no payload is a protocol violation [MQTT-3.8.3-3].

requirements.text: SUBACK MUST repeat the SUBSCRIBE Packet Identifier and return one code per filter.

source_ref.quote: The SUBACK Packet MUST have the same Packet Identifier as the SUBSCRIBE Packet that it is acknowledging [MQTT-3.8.4-2]. […] The payload contains a list of return codes. Each return code corresponds to a Topic Filter in the SUBSCRIBE Packet being acknowledged. The order of return codes in the SUBACK Packet MUST match the order of Topic Filters in the SUBSCRIBE Packet [MQTT-3.9.3-1].

requirements.text: UNSUBSCRIBE MUST contain a non-zero Packet Identifier and one or more Topic Filters.

source_ref.quote: SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, and PUBLISH (in cases where QoS > 0) Control Packets MUST contain a non-zero 16-bit Packet Identifier [MQTT-2.3.1-1]. […] The Payload of an UNSUBSCRIBE packet MUST contain at least one Topic Filter. An UNSUBSCRIBE packet with no payload is a protocol violation [MQTT-3.10.3-2].

requirements.text: The broker MUST send UNSUBACK with the request Packet Identifier even if no subscription was removed.

source_ref.quote: The Server MUST respond to an UNSUBSUBCRIBE request by sending an UNSUBACK packet. The UNSUBACK Packet MUST have the same Packet Identifier as the UNSUBSCRIBE Packet [MQTT-3.10.4-4]. Even where no Topic Subscriptions are deleted, the Server MUST respond with an UNSUBACK [MQTT-3.10.4-5].

requirements.text: The broker MUST answer PINGREQ with PINGRESP; both packets have Remaining Length zero.

source_ref.section: 3.12.1 PINGREQ Fixed header; 3.12.4 Response; 3.13.1 PINGRESP Fixed header
source_ref.quote: byte 2 Remaining Length (0) […] The Server MUST send a PINGRESP Packet in response to a PINGREQ Packet [MQTT-3.12.4-1]. […] byte 2 Remaining Length (0)

requirements.text: DISCONNECT is the client's final packet on the network connection.

source_ref.quote: The DISCONNECT Packet is the final Control Packet sent from the Client to the Server.

requirements.text: The first packet from a client MUST be CONNECT and a client MUST NOT send a second CONNECT on the same connection.

source_ref.quote: After a Network Connection is established by a Client to a Server, the first Packet sent from the Client to the Server MUST be a CONNECT Packet [MQTT-3.1.0-1]. […] A Client can only send the CONNECT Packet once over a Network Connection. The Server MUST process a second CONNECT Packet sent from a Client as a protocol violation and disconnect the Client [MQTT-3.1.0-2].

requirements.text: A broker MUST forward each selected QoS 0 publication to matching connected subscriptions.

source_ref.quote: The Server uses a PUBLISH Packet to send an Application Message to each Client which has a matching subscription. […] When a Server takes ownership of an incoming Application Message it MUST add it to the Session state of those clients that have matching Subscriptions. Matching rules are defined in Section 4.7 [MQTT-4.5.0-1].

requirements.text: A protocol violation MUST close the affected Network Connection unless a packet-specific rule applies.

source_ref.quote: Unless stated otherwise, if either the Server or Client encounters a protocol violation, it MUST close the Network Connection on which it received that Control Packet which caused the protocol violation [MQTT-4.8.0-1].

requirements.text: For non-zero Keep Alive the broker MUST disconnect after 1.5 times the interval without a packet; zero disables this timeout.

source_ref.quote: If the Keep Alive value is non-zero and the Server does not receive a Control Packet from the Client within one and a half times the Keep Alive time period, it MUST disconnect the Network Connection to the Client as if the network had failed [MQTT-3.1.2-24]. […] A Keep Alive value of zero (0) has the effect of turning off the keep alive mechanism. This means that, in this case, the Server is not required to disconnect the Client on the grounds of inactivity.
